Subject: Telemetry filtering & sample logs — follow-up and evidence request

Hi Sam — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

1) Summary of ask: CareQ wants confirmation that request/response logging and headers will not leak PHI (patient name, MRN, SSN) and that trace identifiers and cookies can be masked or hashed. Also need to understand retention windows and evidence for procurement.

2) What we'll deliver by EOD tomorrow (attachments included):
   - A short controls sheet with our configurable logging knobs (Telem-Controls-Quicksheet.pdf)
   - A small sample of sanitized logs showing header scrubbing and hashed trace IDs (sample-sanitized-logs.txt)
   - FAQ on PII handling and our SOC2-log commitments (PII-handling-FAQ.docx / SOC2-section-logs.pdf)

3) Asks for CareQ: please confirm whether you need a short HHS/HIPAA-specific attestation, and whether your procurement team requires a sample S3 bucket with anonymized records for validation. If you can share a single sample event format (JSON) we can produce a sanitized artifact that mirrors your schema.

Next steps / owners:
- Karthik: coordinate delivery and remain the primary contact for procurement (me)
- Monica: produce sanitized log sample and proposed header allowlist (monica)
- Neha: provide a short security note on hashing/lookup policies and retention defaults (neha)

If that all looks right, I’ll send the attachments now and we can set a time for a quick POC handoff next week.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Telemetry filtering & sample logs — follow-up and evidence request

Karthik — thanks for the recap and for moving quickly. A few clarifying items from our side: 

- HIPAA scope: yes, we need confirmation that logs will not contain PHI by default. Any identifiers that could map back to a patient (name, MRN, DOB when combined with other fields) must be pseudonymized before landing in long-term storage. Short-lived operational traces are OK but must be rotatable and not used for analytics.
- Trace IDs: we need either deterministic hashing with a tenant-specific salt or a managed pseudonymization layer. Can you confirm which you recommend and if there is a risk of re-identification?
- Retention: procurement wants default retention for request/response logs set to 30 days for production; longer retention must be an explicit config with justification. What controls do you offer for per-tenant retention?
- Evidence: procurement asks for a sanitized sample set that mirrors our payload (we send HL7-like JSON). We can provide an example event this afternoon.

Also, can you flag any third-party vendors involved in log storage (e.g., S3, logging provider)? We require a list for our vendor risk assessment.

Sam Owens
Senior Security & Privacy Manager | CareQ Health
sam.owens@careqhealth.com

Hi Sam — following up with the security perspective. High-level answers below; I can jump on a short call with your team if you want deeper details.

- PHI in logs: Redwood’s default is to avoid persisting full request/response bodies unless explicitly enabled. For hosted customers we provide a configurable allowlist for headers and a denylist for body fields. By default all request/response bodies are sampled and any fields with keys matching common PHI patterns (name, mrn, ssn, dob) are redacted before storage.

- Trace IDs: we recommend tenant-scoped HMAC hashing (SHA-256 with per-tenant salt) for operational traces retained in short-term caches. For logs that persist to storage we surface a pseudonym (hash) and never keep the unhashed value in plain text. This prevents simple correlation across tenants. Re-identification risk is low if salts are managed per-tenant and rotated periodically; we recommend rotation every 90 days for high-sensitivity customers.

- Retention controls: retention is configurable at the tenant level. Default for request/response logs is 30 days (matches your procurement ask); you can set a shorter or longer retention via the console or API but we record a change event and require a documented business justification for >365 days.

- Third-party storage: hosted deployments use AWS S3 in a customer-region bucket behind a Redwood-managed account. For larger customers we offer Dedicated (customer-owned VPC) or Private (on-prem) where storage location is controlled by you. We will provide a vendor list and the relevant SOC2 sections as attachments.

Attachments included: PII-handling-FAQ.docx, SOC2-section-logs.pdf

If you share a sample JSON event, Monica and I will return a sanitized artifact and a short note on the exact regex/allowlist that handled each field.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Telemetry filtering & sample logs — follow-up and evidence request

Sam — thanks, we received the HL7-like sample you uploaded. Attached is a sanitized snippet and a short explanation of each transformation. Below is an inline example showing the original keys (redacted) and the sanitized output.

Original (example event):
{
  "patient": {"name": "Jane Doe", "mrn": "MRN-234598"},
  "visit": {"timestamp": "2027-08-10T22:11:05Z", "department": "cardiology"},
  "request_id": "7c9f8b2a-1d3a-4f01-9a12-6b8e9c2f3a11",
  "headers": {"Cookie": "session=abcd; Path=/", "X-Trace-Id": "7c9f8b2a..."},
  "payload": {"note": "Patient reports chest pain"}
}

Sanitized output we generate for storage (sample-sanitized-logs.txt):
{
  "patient": {"name": "<REDACTED>", "mrn": "<HASH:07a3f1>"},
  "visit": {"timestamp": "2027-08-10T22:11:05Z", "department": "cardiology"},
  "request_id": "<HASH:4b2c9a>",
  "headers": {"Cookie": "<MASKED>", "X-Trace-Id": "<HASH:4b2c9a>"},
  "payload": {"note": "Patient reports chest pain"}
}

Notes on transformations: 
- Names and free-text fields that match PII patterns are redacted by default.
- Identifiers (MRN, request_id, trace) are hashed with a tenant-specific salt and stored as short digests to enable limited correlation inside the tenant without exposing raw values.
- Headers are allowlisted; Cookie and Authorization are masked by default. We can publish your allowlist and the exact regex we use during the POC.

POC proposal: 
1) We will provision a short-lived sandbox in your region with sample ingestion (no live PHI).
2) We will configure tenant-scoped salt hashing and a 30-day retention.
3) We deliver: sanitized sample set, console screenshot of retention config, and a short runbook for your procurement team.

I’ll attach the sanitized sample and a one-page runbook. If you want a short 30-minute session tomorrow to walk procurement/security through the artifacts, Karthik and Neha are available.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
